_comment: Public, synthetic cases for the official-document search (services/doc_search). No model.
Every report sentence is built from the template main.sh writes (script/main.sh validate_reference_bundle, lines cited in `basis`); paths, sample names and digests are invented.
Ground truth is NOT confirmed: every case starts as review.status = 'unreviewed'. A reviewer sets 'accepted' or 'rejected' with name and date. Metrics are reported per review status.

category: positive = a passage filed under the expected kind should come back; coverage_gap = the kind is classified but no passage is filed for it, so the correct system output today is nothing; negative = nothing may come back.

relevant_kinds is the relevance rule: a returned passage is relevant iff it is filed under one of these kinds. preferred_local lists passage ids (without the 'synthetic-' prefix) a reviewer would want first; it is only scored against the local, non-public corpus and is a proposal until reviewed.

design: rule_replicating = the sentence is a main.sh template and only one outcome is possible once classified; independent_ranking = several passages share the kind and grades_local (0..2, provisional) judge which help most, independent of the rule table; phrasing_variant = same meaning, wording main.sh does not produce, testing robustness. grades_local are AI-proposed and provisional until review.

report_items: BWA index at '/data/wes/ref/GRCh38.fa.*' is incomplete: missing or empty .sa, .pac. bwa resolves the reference to this prefix because '/data/wes/ref/GRCh38.fa.bwt' exists, and it never falls back to another naming variant, so an index at the other prefix would not be used. Rebuild it with `bwa index`.

expected.grade_basis: An incomplete index means it must be rebuilt: -a bwtsw is how a human genome is indexed (2); the default IS algorithm fails above 2GB, a likely cause of the incomplete build (2); memory needed for the rebuild (1).

cases.basis: main.sh:1948 template; rule R-BWA-INCOMPLETE. Preferred: the sentence asks for a rebuild, and -a bwtsw is how a human-size reference is indexed.

report_items: BWA index not found: neither '/data/wes/ref/GRCh38.fa.64.bwt' nor '/data/wes/ref/GRCh38.fa.bwt' exists. Run `bwa index` on the reference; the pipeline never builds it.

expected.grade_basis: No index: build one; bwtsw first (2). Algorithm limit and memory are supporting facts (1).

expected.grade_basis: The index is missing: how to create .tbi/.csi (2, 2) and the precondition that the input is bgzip-compressed and sorted (2). CSI option is an alternative (1). Overwriting an existing index does not apply when none exists (0).

cases.basis: main.sh:2116 template; rule R-VCF-INDEX. Preferred: how to build a .tbi (input must be bgzip-compressed and sorted; bcftools index -t). Disputable: the CSI options are also correct answers.

expected.grade_basis: Same name, different length is exactly this failure (2); the VCF contig length field is where the value lives (2); disabling validation is a risk warning, not a fix (1).

expected.grade_basis: No overlapping contigs is this failure (2); the risk warning (1).

report_items: something unexpected happened while reading the resource bundle

cases.basis: A sentence no rule matches: it is still an input (kind unknown) and must retrieve nothing -- no fallback to free search (doc_retrieval.retrieve).
A run with no failed or warning step (like the real completed run cba73e): no query at all.
commands._CHECK_FAMILIES maps it to an input, but curated passages are filed only under resource-check cause kinds (engine.REASON_CURATED_CHECK). With the manual corpus off nothing may come back.
No command ran for this check: excluded with a reason, never a query.
